scrape-parity.name: caddy
scrape-parity.reason: the ingress runs only in prod; nothing locally serves a Caddy admin endpoint to scrape

scrape-parity.name: sity-web
scrape-parity.reason: sity has an ingress route, an ECR repository and a deploy role, but no deploy workflow and no production compose in the sity repo, so nothing ever runs sity-web in prod. A prod job would scrape an address that does not exist and ServiceDown would page forever. Remove this entry in the same change that adds sity's own deploy workflow.

scrape-parity.name: trading-bot-operator-console
scrape-parity.reason: trading-bot has an ingress route, an ECR repository and a manual-dispatch deploy, but nothing runs it: its seven containers need ~10.6 GiB and the host has 8. A prod job would scrape an address that does not exist and ServiceDown would fire forever. Remove the five trading-bot entries together once the host is large enough to run it.

inhibit-siblings.name: 1:AskBudgetExhausted
inhibit-siblings.reason: a spend alert is not caused by the service being down, so ServiceDown must not hide it

inhibit-siblings.name: 1:AskBudgetNearlySpent
inhibit-siblings.reason: a spend alert is not caused by the service being down, so ServiceDown must not hide it

inhibit-siblings.name: 1:UncaughtExceptions
inhibit-siblings.reason: the exception is a routing decision, not a labelling gap: an uncaught exception is usually why the service went down, and ServiceDown says only that it did. Hiding it would drop the one line that names the cause

inhibit-siblings.name: 1:NotificationsConsumerCrashLooping
inhibit-siblings.reason: the exception is a routing decision, not a labelling gap: the crash loop names the failure, where ServiceDown and ServiceUnhealthy name only the symptom. It also decays on its own once the process stops logging, so it does not outlive the outage

inhibit-siblings.name: 2:NotificationsConsumerCrashLooping
inhibit-siblings.reason: the exception is a routing decision, not a labelling gap: the crash loop names the failure, where ServiceDown and ServiceUnhealthy name only the symptom. It also decays on its own once the process stops logging, so it does not outlive the outage

inhibit-siblings.name: 2:GpoolMailPublishFailing
inhibit-siblings.reason: a publish failure is gpool's own producer, not the mailer being unhealthy, so ServiceUnhealthy on notifications must not hide it
